slot.brief: YDSE diagram with labelled slit separation and screen distance; locate a point with given path difference and ask the fringe order/position at that point.

stem: In a YDSE using light of wavelength $500$ nm, point $P$ is located as shown in the figure. Which fringe is formed at $P$? Use the small-angle approximation.

verdicts.working: Path difference: Δ ≈ dy/D = (0.60×10⁻³)(2.5×10⁻³)/2.0 = 0.75×10⁻⁶ m = 1.5λ. This is the second dark fringe.

working:
$$\Delta \simeq \dfrac{dy}{D}=\dfrac{(0.60\times10^{-3})(2.5\times10^{-3})}{2.0}=7.5\times10^{-7}\ \text{m}=1.5\lambda$$
$$\Delta=(n+\tfrac12)\lambda,\quad n=1\;\Rightarrow\;\text{second dark fringe}$$

Independent check: Path difference: Δ ≈ dy/D = (0.60×10⁻³)(2.5×10⁻³)/2.0 = 0.75×10⁻⁶ m = 1.5λ. This is the second dark fringe.

draft.stem: In a YDSE using light of wavelength $500$ nm, point $P$ is located as shown in the figure. Which fringe is formed at $P$? Use the small-angle approximation.

figure.description: Draw two narrow vertical slits S1 and S2 on the left, separated vertically by d = 0.60 mm. Draw a vertical screen to their right, with the screen distance from the midpoint between the slits labelled D = 2.0 m. Mark O on the screen on the horizontal line through the slit midpoint. Mark P on the screen 2.5 mm above O and label OP = y. Show the horizontal central axis from the slit midpoint to O.

draft.distractor_notes: A: treats $1.5\lambda$ as the first dark fringe. C: treats a half-integer path difference as constructive interference. D: mistakes $1.5\lambda$ for $3\lambda$.
